option_checks.evidence: Nonnormal incidence has coplanar incident/reflected paths and local normal, with geometric paths on opposite sides of normal; exception is explicitly qualified.
The standard incidence/reflection angles are measured from the normal, not the tangent surface. Equal complementary surface angles do not make this definition correct.
Nonnormal reflected path is on the opposite, not the same, side of the normal in the incidence plane.
Both angles are defined from the same local normal and are equal; this also holds at normal incidence.
The incident-normal and reflected-normal planes coincide at nonnormal incidence, rather than being perpendicular.
Normal incidence gives both normal-based angles zero and reverse travel along the incident line.
Concave/convex actual-versus-extension behavior and real/virtual focus identities are swapped.
Convex reflected rays diverge on the incident side; no actual ray intersection forms a real focus behind the mirror.
Parallel-to-principal-axis rays define actual concave convergence in front and convex backward-extension virtual convergence behind, under stated paraxial approximation.
Curvature center determines local radius normals, not the common principal-focus position of an axis-parallel bundle. Identifying these distinct points is false for finite spherical mirrors.
